titleEn: Droid scales up: new FD60 brings autonomous seeding and weeding to larger farms
titleZh: FarmDroid推出FD60大型田间机器人：自主播种与除草能力扩展至大型农场
summaryZh: 丹麦农业机器人公司FarmDroid推出大型田间机器人FD60，具备自主播种和机械除草功能，无需除草剂和人工操作。该机器人是FD20的升级版，作业能力约为其3倍，日作业面积达18公顷，季节作业能力达60公顷，每公顷成本低至304欧元。FD60采用RTK GPS定位技术，播种时记录每粒种子的精确位置，除草时按坐标导航，无需摄像头和图像识别。支持洋葱、甜菜、玉米等100多种行栽作物，太阳能供电，可24小时连续作业。
featuredReason: 该新闻展示了田间机器人从技术验证走向规模化商业应用的关键突破，其基于GPS坐标而非视觉的除草方案在成本、可靠性和适应性上具有显著创新性，对智慧农业领域的自动化技术选型具有重要参考价值。

The machine was launched on 1 September 2026. The FD60 is the big sibling of the FD20 – with roughly 3 times the seasonal capacity. Where the FD20 targets smaller operations, the FD60 is built for scale: up to 6.75 metres working width, up to 20 rows in a single pass, and a seasonal capacity of 60 hectares. Daily output reaches up to 18 hectares – three times the FD20’s 6 hectares per day. “For years, what held field robots back wasn’t the technology”, FarmDroid emphasises. “It was the cost per hectare, which kept them in the few crops that could carry it.” The FD60 is designed to change that equation, the company says, with a cost as low as €304 per hectare across a full season, replacing manual weeding hours, chemical inputs, and most of the fuel cost of a conventional tractor. !Image 7: The new FarmDroid is compatible with onions, beet, maize, green beans, endives, chicory, spinach, and more than 100 other row crops. The new FarmDroid is compatible with onions, beet, maize, green beans, endives, chicory, spinach, and more than 100 other row crops. How it works The FD60 follows a simple four-step process: set up, seed, weed, refuel. During seeding, the robot records the exact GPS position of every seed using RTK GPS with 8 mm precision. When it returns to weed, it navigates back to those same coordinates and removes the weeds mechanically – both between the rows and between individual plants within the row, where a camera-guided machine cannot safely reach. There are no cameras, no crop-recognition software, and nothing to calibrate or train. Because the robot knows exactly where it planted each seed, it does not need to see the crop to avoid damaging it. According to FarmDroid, the approach also eliminates a common failure point of vision-based weeding systems: dust, low light, and variable crop appearance cannot confuse a system that works from coordinates rather than images. Working width and wheel spacing are adjustable rather than fixed, allowing the FD60 to adapt to different row layouts. Row spacing starts from 25 cm, and wheel spacing can be set anywhere between 4.60 and 6.70 metres. !Image 8: During seeding, the robot records the exact GPS position of every seed using RTK GPS with 8 mm precision. When it returns to weed, it navigates back to those same coordinates and removes the weeds mechanically. During seeding, the robot records the exact GPS position of every seed using RTK GPS with 8 mm precision. When it returns to weed, it navigates back to those same coordinates and removes the weeds mechanically. Crops and markets The FD60 is compatible with onions, beet, maize, green beans, endives, chicory, spinach, and more than 100 other row crops. It is suited to both organic and conventional operations – for organic growers because it eliminates herbicides entirely, and for conventional growers because it reduces chemical inputs and labour costs on the most demanding field jobs. “Labour is hard to find here, so keeping manual work to a minimum matters”, says Anton Maier, an organic sugar beet grower in Germany who has been using FarmDroid since 2020. “FarmDroid has worked very well, and whenever I needed help, I could always reach someone quickly by phone.” Seeding and weeding are the season’s most labour-intensive tasks. The FD60 takes both on autonomously, freeing staff for other work during the busiest periods of the growing calendar. The FD60 is designed to stay in the field throughout the season. Power Power comes from eight solar panels producing 3.7 kW, feeding a 23.5 kWh lithium battery. When solar input falls short – in overcast conditions or during extended night operation – a Range Extender generator (3 kW, 12-litre petrol tank) tops the battery up. The battery level is visible in the FarmDroid app, and the operator refuels when it suits them, keeping the machine running up to 24 hours a day. !Image 9: FarmDroid claims the FD60 can bring the cost of seeding and weeding down to as little as €304 per hectare across a full season – replacing manual labour, chemical inputs, and most of the fuel a conventional tractor would consume. FarmDroid claims the FD60 can bring the cost of seeding and weeding down to as little as €304 per hectare across a full season – replacing manual labour, chemical inputs, and most of the fuel a conventional tractor would consume. The platform already has a proven track record: FarmDroid says more than 500 robots based on the same platform have been operating in 26 countries since 2018.. FarmDroid positions local dealer support as a core part of the product. Each installation is handled by a local partner who sets up the machine with the grower and remains available through the season. The FarmDroid app includes an AI assistant called Odin for day-to-day questions, with the local partner and FarmDroid team reachable directly for more complex issues. Orders open on 1 September 2026. First deliveries are expected from January 2027. The FD60 can be seen in person at Agromek in Herning, Denmark, 24 to 27 November 2026. !Image 10: Power comes from eight solar panels producing 3.7 kW, feeding a 23.5 kWh lithium battery. translationZh:
丹麦农业机器人公司FarmDroid推出了FD60，这是一款专为自主播种和机械除草设计的大型田间机器人，可在不使用除草剂且无需操作员在场的情况下完成作业。该机器于2026年9月1日发布。

FD60是FD20的“大号兄弟”——季节作业能力约为后者的3倍。FD20面向小型农场，而FD60专为规模化作业而生：作业宽度可达6.75米，单次通过最多可覆盖20行，季节作业能力达60公顷。日作业量最高可达18公顷，是FD20（日作业6公顷）的3倍。

“多年来，制约田间机器人的不是技术本身，”FarmDroid强调，“而是每公顷成本，这使机器人只能局限于少数能承担得起该成本的作物。”FarmDroid表示，FD60旨在改变这一局面，全季每公顷成本可低至304欧元，替代了人工除草工时、化学投入以及传统拖拉机的大部分燃料成本。

**工作原理**

FD60遵循一个简单的四步流程：设置、播种、除草、加油。播种时，机器人利用RTK GPS以8毫米的精度记录每粒种子的精确GPS位置。返回除草时，它导航至相同的坐标，以机械方式清除杂草——既包括行间杂草，也包括行内单株作物之间的杂草，而后者是摄像头引导的机器无法安全触及的区域。

没有摄像头，没有作物识别软件，也无需校准或训练。由于机器人确切知道每粒种子的播种位置，它无需“看见”作物即可避免损伤作物。据FarmDroid称，这种方法还消除了基于视觉的除草系统的一个常见故障点：灰尘、弱光和变化的作物外观无法干扰一个基于坐标而非图像运行的系统。

作业宽度和轮距均可调节而非固定不变，使FD60能够适应不同的行距布局。行距最小从25厘米起，轮距可在4.60米至6.70米之间任意设置。

**作物与市场**

FD60兼容洋葱、甜菜、玉米、青豆、菊苣、苦菊、菠菜以及100多种其他行栽作物。它适用于有机和常规种植——对有机种植者而言，因为它完全消除了除草剂的使用；对常规种植者而言，因为它减少了在最繁重田间作业中的化学投入和人工成本。

“这里很难找到劳动力，因此将人工工作量降至最低至关重要，”德国有机甜菜种植者Anton Maier表示，他自2020年以来一直在使用FarmDroid。“FarmDroid表现非常好，每当我需要帮助时，总能通过电话迅速联系到人。”

播种和除草是季节中劳动强度最大的两项任务。FD60自主承担这两项工作，在种植日历最繁忙的时期将人力解放出来从事其他工作。FD60的设计目标是在整个季节中持续驻留田间。

**动力系统**

动力来自八块太阳能板，总输出功率3.7千瓦，为一块23.5千瓦时的锂电池供电。当太阳能输入不足时——例如阴天或长时间夜间作业时——一台增程发电机（输出功率3千瓦，配12升汽油箱）为电池补充电力。电池电量可在FarmDroid应用程序中查看，操作员可根据自身方便的时间加油，使机器可连续运行长达24小时。

该平台已有良好的实际应用记录：FarmDroid表示，自2018年以来，已有超过500台基于同一平台的机器人在26个国家投入运行。

FarmDroid将本地经销商支持定位为产品的核心组成部分。每次安装均由本地合作伙伴负责，他们会与种植者一起完成机器设置，并在整个季节中持续提供服务。FarmDroid应用程序内置了一款名为Odin的AI助手，用于解答日常问题；遇到更复杂的问题时，可直接联系本地合作伙伴和FarmDroid团队。

订单于2026年9月1日开放。首批交付预计从2027年1月开始。FD60将于2026年11月24日至27日在丹麦海宁的Agromek展会上进行现场展示。
